newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SOCCER-INJURY RULES THREE PLAYERS OUT OF AUSTRIA SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INJURY RULES THREE PLAYERS OUT OF AUSTRIA SQUAD.

text.p: Injury ruled three players out of Austria's squad on Friday for next Wednesday's important World Cup group four qualifier against Scotland.

Werder Bremen forward Heimo Pfeifenberger is nursing a broken toe, 1860 Munich's Harald Cerny injured his right ankle in Thursday's Bundesliga match against VfB Stuttgart while Linzer ASK defender Goran Kartalija has calf pains.
Coach Herbert Prohaska has replaced Pfeifenberger with Austria Vienna striker Andreas Ogris, Cerny with Casino Graz's Dieter Ramusch while Sturm Graz's Roman Maehlich will replace Kartalija.
Prohaska already had to do without midfielders Dietmar Kuehbauer of Rapid Vienna and the injured Adi Huetter of SV Salzburg when he named his 18-man squad on Thursday.
Kuehbauer asked not to be considered after opting to stay in Austria with his wife Michaela who is currently in a coma following a car crash.
Prohaska told a news conference on Friday: "There is no point in sulking, we will have to do with what we have."
Despite the setbacks, Huetter is the only player missing from the team which scored a surprise 1-0 group four victory over Sweden in Stockholm last October.
Austria are currently second in the group standings, a point behind Scotland and a point ahead of Sweden.
But they had their confidence badly shaken 10 days ago when they lost their first international since November 1995 -- a shock 2-0 defeat by Slovenia in Linz.
Goalkeepers: Michael Konsel (Rapid Vienna), Franz Wohlfahrt (VfB Stuttgart)

Defenders: Wolfgang Feiersinger (Borussia Dortmund), Michael Hatz (AC Reggiana), Roman Maehlich (Sturm Graz), Walter Kogler (SV Salzburg), Anton Pfeffer (Austria Vienna), Peter Schoettel (Rapid Vienna)
Midfielders: Franz Aigner (SV Salzburg), Andreas Heraf (Rapid Vienna), Andreas Herzog (Werder Bremen), Markus Schopp (Hamburg), Peter Stoeger (Rapid Vienna)
Forwards: Andreas Ogris (Austria Vienna), Dieter Ramusch (Casino Graz), Anton Polster (Cologne), Ivica Vastic (Sturm Graz), Arnold Wetl (FC Porto)
